description: Ordered work sessions and dependency gates for the audited chess-coach plan. Estimates are focused hours, not guaranteed calendar days.

tasks.title: Reproducible local environment and baseline tests
steps: Create an isolated Python environment and pin tested runtime dependencies; keep training packages separate.
Document Windows setup, Stockfish installation/discovery and example environment-variable names without reading or copying real keys.
Create README setup commands; preserve existing scripts/data and record known prototype failures.
acceptance: A fresh environment imports the required libraries and runs the existing workflow tests.
Tests reject a missing/invalid engine configuration with an actionable error rather than a hard-coded user path.
Evidence lists the actual interpreter, dependency versions, setup commands and their results.

tasks.title: Strict PGN parsing and legal position replay
steps: Add a shared PGN parser with one-game, UTF-8, 256-KB and 200-ply limits; treat parser errors as errors.
Support legal standard-chess setup FENs and preserve move history; reject unsupported variants and illegal mainlines.
Add small original PGN fixtures for White/Black review, comments, castling, en passant, promotion, terminal and repetition cases.
acceptance: Every emitted FEN and SAN/UCI pair agrees with legal replay; learner decisions are pre-move positions.
Malformed, multiple-game, invalid-position and oversize submissions fail clearly.
Comments and future moves never become instructions or current-position context.

tasks.title: Versioned analysis records and score orientation
steps: Implement AnalysisRecord, Candidate, CoachingCard and TrainingExample schemas with stable IDs/versioning.
Represent centipawn, mate and unavailable scores explicitly; normalize to the learner before any subtraction.
Keep search provenance, position/history references and played-move evidence distinct.
acceptance: White/Black score tests catch sign reversal after a move.
Mate scores cannot be silently converted to centipawn teaching losses.
Invalid candidate roots, missing provenance and malformed records are rejected.

tasks.title: Persistent Stockfish ownership and lifecycle
steps: Create one engine-owning worker/session using environment/PATH configuration, one thread and bounded hash/search time.
Reuse the process for sequential positions; close it on shutdown, timeout, failure and cancellation.
Use deterministic fake-engine tests plus a separately recorded real-binary smoke run.
acceptance: Two positions reuse one process; shutdown and crash recovery do not leak a child.
Missing binary and timed-out search produce typed actionable failures.
Evidence records the real engine version and a legal smoke-test line; mocks are not reported as that smoke run.

tasks.title: MultiPV candidates and the actual played-move reply
steps: Return up to three legal candidate lines, with score/PV drawn from the same search result.
If the played move is absent, add a restricted-root search and retain the opponent's strongest reply.
Record time/depth/nodes and flag inconsistent or unstable comparisons; preserve full PVs internally.
acceptance: A deliberately bad move outside MultiPV still has its own line and evaluation.
Illegal/mismatched PV roots fail validation, including mate and terminal positions.
Near-equal or unstable candidates do not become categorical mistakes.

tasks.title: Deterministic board facts and evidence references
steps: Compute material, legal checks/captures, attacks, pins, open files and simple pawn-structure facts.
Compute changes along candidate lines and reference exact line/ply for concrete claims.
Keep attack counts separate from verified hanging-piece or winning-tactic claims.
acceptance: Original fixed-board fixtures cover a pinned defender, defended attacked piece, opening file and passed pawn.
A board fact is evaluated at its referenced position, not the unrelated root.
Unsupported tactical conclusions remain unknown instead of being asserted.

tasks.title: Opening explorer with honest statistics and caching
steps: Implement exact-position Masters and rating-filtered Lichess lookups using documented endpoints.
Serialize calls, cache responses, set timeouts, handle rate limits and disclose sample size/source/filters.
Keep common moves and named openings separate from proven superiority; respect the initial move-window/sparse-sample defaults.
acceptance: Transpositions match by position; SAN membership elsewhere cannot classify a book move.
Mocked timeout, sparse data, invalid JSON and HTTP 429 produce bounded failures/fallbacks.
The reviewed opening context contains no later game moves; popularity alone never creates a best-move claim.

tasks.title: Tablebase eligibility and draw-rule context
steps: Add a small tablebase adapter with supported-piece-count/castling eligibility and visible engine fallback.
Preserve fifty-move/repetition context, rule-dependent outcomes and score perspective.
Keep distance-to-zeroing separate from mate distance.
acceptance: Unsupported positions do not make tablebase calls.
Rule-dependent wins/draws and unavailable responses are represented without a false forced-mate claim.
Mocks cover timeout and malformed responses; terminal positions avoid pointless searches.

tasks.title: Whole-game scan and instructive-moment selection
steps: Scan only learner decisions with bounded preliminary searches; deep-confirm selected moments.
Prioritize meaningful losses, forcing choices, strong decisions and opening moments; deduplicate adjacent repeated lessons.
Return at most fifteen, show the top three first, and allow zero/fewer moments without padding.
acceptance: Synthetic score traces deterministically select known turning points and reject noisy near-equalities.
Short and quiet games do not fabricate ten cards; both colors work.
Selected explanations use deep evidence and the actual played line, not shallow scores alone.

tasks.title: Replaceable model client with OpenRouter free-only option
steps: Implement generate_card behind a small hosted/Ollama interface; use HTTP facilities already installed.
Support a configurable explicit OpenRouter free model and recorded provider; fetch/catalog-check zero pricing before calls.
Disable automatic paid fallback; separate unavailable/429/invalid-response errors; keep keys server-side and out of logs.
acceptance: Mocked paid/unknown pricing, missing keys and unavailable free endpoints fail closed.
Tests assert the exact requested model/provider and safe structured request contents.
No live request is required for offline tests; live smoke evidence is separately labeled and only run with configured credentials.

tasks.title: Grounded card prompts and response validation
steps: Serialize compact evidence and prefix-only game context; include candidate and played-move continuations.
Request detailed structured cards with short summary, comparisons, replayable references, lesson and uncertainty.
Validate schema, referenced moves/facts and token budgets; allow one repair, then suppress invalid output.
acceptance: A legal line paired with a false concrete board claim is rejected by supported-fact checks.
Prompt-injection comments, invented intent, wrong-side scores and unknown line references are caught in fixtures.
Uncheckable strategic interpretation is qualified; the validator does not claim complete semantic proof.

tasks.title: One-card end-to-end integration and ten-position suite
steps: Wire parser -> engine -> evidence -> model -> validator -> card through one shared pipeline.
Use ten original curated positions spanning tactics, quiet play, alternatives, openings and endgames.
Migrate the prototype entrypoint after callers/tests work; remove duplicated phase analysis without dropping error handling.
acceptance: Offline integration uses deterministic model/engine fixtures and produces replayable cards.
Optional live smoke results clearly name the real engine/model; simulated output is never presented as generated evidence.
A bad model response is suppressed while preserving an actionable error.

tasks.title: SQLite review jobs, bounded queue and cancellation
steps: Add persistent job status, one bounded in-process queue and a single engine worker.
Add capability tokens, cancellation, timeouts and failed-on-restart recovery.
Keep runtime reports separate from source and annotation projects; clean up resources on every exit.
acceptance: Queue overflow, wrong token, cancellation and engine/model failure have explicit states.
Restart never leaves an in-progress job polling forever.
Concurrent submissions cannot overlap searches in one engine or corrupt stored status.

tasks.title: Local FastAPI upload and progress interface
steps: Build server-rendered upload/paste form with learner-color selection and browser-local PGN recovery.
Add POST /reviews and token-protected status/progress endpoints with clear validation messages.
Keep headers/comments out of model instructions and render all user strings safely.
acceptance: HTTP tests cover valid upload, paste, missing color, malformed/oversize PGN and unauthorized review access.
Progress and reset/retry behavior survive a failed job without exposing another report.
Document a real browser smoke check; no external hosting yet.

tasks.title: Interactive report board and detailed coaching cards
steps: Bundle a pinned board component and documented piece assets; display orientation, move list and replayable supplied variations.
Show the first three moments and expandable remaining cards; preserve detailed explanations.
Add keyboard navigation, visible notation, responsive layout and empty/error states.
acceptance: Tests check generated board states, orientation, line/ply mapping and HTML escaping.
Browser evidence covers keyboard navigation, mobile-width layout and both colors.
Board reset returns to the reviewed position; arbitrary unevaluated variation chat is not implied.

tasks.title: Feedback, retention and provider disclosures
steps: Add helpful/not-helpful, issue category and optional comment per card.
Add explicit contribution opt-in, header stripping before remote calls, 24-hour ordinary-report expiry and reset.
Keep annotation projects until deliberate removal; block public reviewer routes and avoid secrets/raw PGNs in logs.
acceptance: Opting out does not create training examples; opting in creates untrusted feedback awaiting review.
Expired/wrong-token reviews cannot be read or edited; identity headers do not reach the mocked provider.
Deletion/expiry preserves deliberate annotation projects and has tests preventing cross-project deletion.

tasks.title: Local acceptance, failure recovery and performance report
steps: Run the complete offline suite and a separate real-provider/engine acceptance run when credentials exist.
Measure twenty representative games; record p50/p95, engine/model versions, cache state, per-stage latency and failures.
Document fresh-install and browser acceptance outcomes; fix acceptance-blocking failures before completion.
acceptance: Evidence includes actual twenty-game results, not an estimate or mocked latency.
Interrupted jobs, unavailable provider and engine crashes recover without lost resources or endless polling.
If credentials/hardware prevent the real run, block this task with reproducible details rather than mark complete.

tasks.title: Human first-demo and learning review
steps: Have the user review the real demo for correctness, clarity, navigation and useful detail.
Ask at least three target players to review a game and explain one lesson in their own words; user handles invitations.
Record serious errors and fix them through a focused follow-up before approving this gate.
acceptance: Evidence contains real reviewer observations and game/card references, without invented participants.
At least one simple transfer exercise is attempted; report limitations rather than claiming rating improvement.
Human approval explicitly says whether the local demo is ready for portfolio preparation.

tasks.title: Local annotation interface and immutable revisions
steps: Reuse the board/report UI to inspect evidence, edit coaching fields and approve/reject revisions.
Store drafts, reviewer identity, revision history and approved outputs separately from immutable analysis.
Keep the interface local-only and export only approved current revisions.
acceptance: Editing a card never overwrites its analysis or original draft.
Rejected, empty and unapproved records cannot enter an export.
Tests cover revision history, stale edits and local-only reviewer routes.

tasks.title: Streaming corpus sampler, provenance and locked splits
steps: Replace all-games-in-memory sampling with streaming PGN ingestion and reproducible sampling.
Record source/license/game hash, canonical position and theme; partition before generating labels.
Keep games and transposed duplicate positions together or omit collisions; preserve an untouched test set and pilot separation.

Implement python -m coach.dataset audit-batch --batch L01 --expected-count 25 --partition train (and other batch IDs/partitions). Return nonzero for missing/incorrect counts, unapproved or empty labels, wrong themes/partitions, reused IDs, missing provenance or unresolved critical claims; emit the audited ID list and manifest hash.
acceptance: Fixtures containing duplicate games/transpositions cannot leak positions across splits.
Streaming output is deterministic with a seed and handles empty/bad source games without losing progress.
Existing six prototype labels remain unchanged and excluded; train/validation/test manifests are independently auditable.

tasks.title: Human review of draft-source and provider permissions
steps: Choose an explicit model/provider for drafts and document current terms for inputs, outputs, synthetic training and distribution.
Distinguish provider use of your prompts from permission for you to train on its outputs; free price alone proves neither.
If permission is unclear, approve original human-authored labels or an explicitly permitted local source instead.
acceptance: Evidence names the exact provider/model, checked URLs/date, allowed purpose and constraints.
Approval states which source is allowed for training drafts and which may only be used as a runtime/evaluation baseline.
An agent cannot self-approve unclear rights or assume OpenRouter bypasses underlying restrictions.

tasks.title: Resumable draft generation with free-tier budgets
steps: Generate candidate cards from approved analysis using the allowed source; preserve raw drafts and request metadata.
Default to at most twenty attempts per session, forty per rolling 24 hours and at least four seconds between calls; count failures/repairs.
Checkpoint each attempt, resume without duplicates, stop on quota exhaustion and never switch silently to paid or unrelated models.
acceptance: Mocked interruptions, duplicate retries, HTTP 429/402 and exhausted budgets preserve progress and never leak keys.
Records store model/provider, prompt/schema/config hashes, source partition and validation status.
No generated draft automatically becomes a gold reference; human-authored input is supported when API reuse is disallowed.

tasks.title: Human thirty-example pilot and independent chess check
steps: Review thirty pilot explanations outside the final 500, spanning all four themes and both strong/error examples.
Have a stronger chess reviewer inspect at least ten difficult examples; user arranges this and records disagreements.
Freeze a practical rubric and revise the evidence/card schema before scaling; measure actual review time.
acceptance: Every accepted pilot answer has real edits/approval and source evidence.
Unsupported claims, ambiguous wording and equivalent moves have recorded resolutions.
Evidence records time per accepted answer and whether scaling is justified; no synthetic reviewer signatures.

tasks.title: Explanation evaluation harness and blind rating exports
steps: Build automatic legality/fact/schema checks plus separate 1-5 human rubrics for correctness, support, clarity and usefulness.
Blind/randomize model outputs, hide reference answers from generation, and aggregate ratings/error counts with uncertainty notes.
Use validation for selection and reserve test for the final locked configuration; do not use one model as the sole judge.
acceptance: Known illegal, wrong-side, invented-material and false-fact examples are flagged.
Test answers cannot appear in generation prompts or optimization inputs.
Score summaries preserve denominators, reviewer disagreement and missing ratings rather than reporting false accuracy.

tasks.title: Portfolio package and reproducible local release
steps: Write clean installation/use documentation, a short demo recording/script, architecture glossary and measured limitations.
Include reproducible acceptance results and a small rights-cleared sample; prepare resume wording with actual measured facts.
Verify a fresh install and document current license/provenance decisions; do not publish externally in this task.
acceptance: A new reader can run a sample review from documented commands.
All performance/quality/adoption claims link to actual evidence; missing measures are explicitly absent.
Smoke tests verify the documented local entrypoint and sample data.

tasks.title: Review label batch 1/20: 25 train examples
steps: Review 25 new approved examples: opening decisions; partition=train. Draw replacements only from the same locked partition/theme.
Replay best and played continuations, check every concrete claim, edit for detailed club-player teaching, then approve each record.
Record accepted IDs, rejected/replaced IDs, review time and difficult claims for a stronger-player check.
acceptance: Exactly 25 new, nonempty, approved current revisions are listed; none duplicates an earlier batch or the pilot.
The dataset audit passes provenance, schema, split and evidence-reference checks; do not train or tune on test examples.
Human evidence links the batch export/audit and lists unresolved claims; unresolved examples are not accepted.

tasks.title: Baseline models, memory and conversion smoke benchmark
steps: Benchmark untuned OLMo 2 7B Instruct, Qwen3 4B and the allowed hosted baseline on validation only.
Measure local memory/speed, schema success and blind-review outputs with pinned model/tokenizer/config revisions.
Smoke-test export/import compatibility before selecting the candidate with fewer severe errors, then usefulness, then local speed.
acceptance: Evidence contains real model outputs and hardware measurements, not package-size estimates.
All models receive the same evidence and no reference answers; test partition remains untouched.
Unavailable hardware/model endpoints block the task or produce explicitly partial research, not a claimed winning model.

tasks.title: Human compute and training-run approval
steps: Choose an available environment whose terms permit this workload; clarify Colab's chess-training restriction before relying on it.
Verify GPU memory/capacity, dataset permissions, checkpoint storage and any hard spending limit.
Record the exact approved training configuration and resume/storage plan.
acceptance: Evidence establishes an actual permitted compute path, not a promise of free GPU access.
At least a tiny memory/setup smoke run fits without silent example truncation.
The user explicitly approves any paid compute; otherwise this gate stays incomplete.

tasks.title: Reproducible QLoRA training and checkpoint selection
steps: Implement a pinned notebook/script for supervised QLoRA using the plan's conservative initial settings.
Use only the 400 training records, validate on the 50 validation records, checkpoint and persist seeds/configs/logs.
Count tokens for actual tokenizer/input/output; reject or deliberately narrow oversize examples instead of silently truncating.
acceptance: Dry-run tests prove split isolation, label masking, complete token coverage and deterministic data order.
Evidence includes an actual training run, selected checkpoint and validation rationale; a notebook alone is insufficient.
Interrupted execution resumes from a valid checkpoint without secretly changing the data/config.

tasks.title: Locked held-out model evaluation
steps: Lock model/checkpoint/prompts, then generate tuned/base/hosted outputs on the fifty held-out examples once.
Run automatic checks, blind the outputs and export human rating forms without leaking references into generation.
Record errors, failures, latency and sample-size limitations; changing the model after viewing test results requires a new independent test set.
acceptance: Assertions catch any held-out content in training inputs or checkpoints' data manifests.
Every result has model revision and configuration provenance, including failures.
Metrics distinguish automatic facts from human judgments and report counts, not unsupported broad competence claims.

tasks.title: Human blind model comparison and release decision
steps: Rate blinded held-out outputs against the chess evidence using the frozen rubric.
Have a second qualified reviewer check difficult/severe claims and record disagreement.
Decide whether the fine-tune improves usefulness without increasing critical errors; accept a negative result honestly.
acceptance: Evidence contains actual ratings and an unblinding record.
Release examples contain no known unresolved critical error; uncertainty from fifty examples is stated.
Approval specifies which model remains the product default and why; fine-tuned status alone is not a pass.

tasks.title: Ollama quantization and post-export regression
steps: Merge/convert the selected permitted model to supported GGUF, quantize for 16 GB RAM, and create an Ollama model definition.
Preserve adapter, model/config/license revisions and reproducible conversion commands.
Repeat validation and a fresh acceptance sample after quantization; integrate only if the human-selected default warrants it.
acceptance: Real local requests produce valid replayable cards and recorded memory/latency.
Post-quantization errors are compared with the pre-export model; regressions are not hidden.
If a fine-tune was rejected, package the approved baseline or document the negative experiment without falsely calling it a deployed fine-tune.

tasks.title: Open-source release candidate and license inventory
steps: Prepare reproducible source, evaluation examples, contribution guidance and a license/provenance inventory for code/models/assets/data.
Document engine/model download steps without committing keys, runtime databases or giant generated weights.
Create a local release checklist and minimal fresh-install check; external publication remains a separate approval.
acceptance: Rights/attribution entries cover python-chess, Stockfish, board pieces, models and sample data.
Tracked file scan finds no credentials, private submissions or unapproved label exports.
A fresh install can run the sample/offline checks; inaccessible services are disclosed.

tasks.title: Human invited-beta destination and publication approval
steps: Choose a currently available hosting/storage/provider combination within the actual budget.
Review provider eligibility, audience, retention, external-data handling, quotas and admin-route isolation.
Record exact target accounts/URLs and explicit authorization for publication; unlisted URLs still need abuse controls.
acceptance: Evidence identifies real accounts/destinations and provider availability.
The user explicitly authorizes the external publish action and configured data processing.
Credentials are configured privately; no imaginary free production capacity or approvals.

tasks.title: Hosted-beta configuration and deployment verification
steps: Add the minimum deployment configuration for the approved destination and durable opt-in feedback.
Implement request/global quotas, review tokens, bounded work, expiry, retry-later failure and operator disable.
Deploy only to the approved destination and verify real anonymous-user access, cold starts and disabled reviewer routes.
acceptance: Tests cover quotas, private review access, expiry, restart failure and provider unavailability.
Evidence records actual deployment URL, build/config revision, smoke results and rollback/disable procedure.
No publication beyond the approved scope; unavailable free hosting leaves a documented blocker.

tasks.title: Human four-week beta feedback and learning review
steps: Invite 15-20 target testers through the user; collect consenting feedback and weekly return counts.
Review comprehension/transfer exercises, serious errors, completion/dropoff and real cost per completed review.
Decide whether to iterate, keep it as a portfolio tool, or investigate a narrow paid use case.
acceptance: Evidence uses actual counts and consented observations, including inactive users and failures.
No invented users, rating gains, revenue or retention.
Public bugs produce focused follow-up tasks; feedback never auto-promotes itself to training truth.

tasks.title: Human optional startup discovery and paid-pilot decision
steps: Interview ten players and three coaches about recent problems, tools and spending; the user handles outreach.
Compare a narrow coach/student workflow with existing alternatives and measure a concrete willingness-to-pay test.
Document whether paid pilots, repeat use and operating economics justify business work; otherwise close the portfolio scope.
acceptance: Evidence contains real interview summaries and paid commitments only if they occurred.
Any 60% preference, five week-four returners or three customers are proposed decision signals, never fabricated results.
Decision explicitly says continue, narrow, or stop business expansion.
